result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers build the same 'Bring the flat' campaign across all four forms and stick closely to the fact sheet. A is better because it offers an actual fallback concept for the board, labels its assumptions (the beginner-intimidation tension and the 'hallway' detail), and includes ask-the-owner lines about trial visits and what the walkthrough covers. B has no fallback, and it states an assumption about beginners as fact. Its sign-up placeholders and open items are useful, though. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers build one clear 'Bring the flat' campaign across all four forms and stick to the fact sheet. B is better because it marks its assumptions, puts concrete ask-the-owner questions to the board (for example, whether the walkthrough covers fixing a flat), states the beginner's worry directly and gives the fallback concept the rubric asks for. A has neither a fallback nor much framing of why people hesitate, and its claim that many people have never used a bike stand is an unflagged assumption.
